subject: Plotting a tree - collapsing a vector of nodes

messages.author: 752aaa009ee55b1c
messages.subject: Plotting a tree - collapsing a vector of nodes
parts:
Dear Dr. Yu,

Thank you for making ggtree available to worldwide researchers and students, it is a great tool and I am moving my first steps with it.

As I work with large trees, I am trying to collapse nodes iteratively, but with no luck. Please find  example below:

tempnwk<- "((('clade01_1':1.35E-4,('clade01_2':1.0E-6,'clade01_3':1.0E-6):3.3E-5):3.3E-5,('clade02_1':2.7E-4,'clade02_2':3.3E-5):3.3E-5):1.0E-6,'clade03_1':1.0E-6);"  
testTree0 <- read.tree(text = tempnwk)
rm(tempnwk)
ggtree(testTree0) +  geom_text(aes(label=node))
ggtree(testTree0) +  geom_text(aes(label=label))

testcollapse0<- ggtree(testTree0)
###This Works
testcollapse0b<- testcollapse0 %>% collapse(node = 10) +
  geom_point2(aes(subset=(node==10)),
              shape=21, size=5, fill='green')
testcollapse0b<- collapse(testcollapse0b, node = 11) +
  geom_point2(aes(subset=(node==11)),
              shape=21, size=5, fill='red')

testcollapse0b ### <-- it works

#############
##This does not work:
nodes2go<- c(10, 11)
myTestCols<- c('green', 'red')
testcollapse1<- testcollapse0
for(i in 1:2) {
  testcollapse1<- testcollapse1 %>% collapse(
    node = nodes2go[i])  +
    geom_point2(
      aes(subset=(node==i)), shape=23,
      size=7, fill=myTestCols[i])
}
rm(i)
testcollapse0 + geom_text(aes(label=label))
testcollapse1 + geom_text(aes(label=label))
#
##
# #Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : object 'i' not found


So far, I have found a workaround:

###How about this:
myTestCols2<- c("'green'", "'red'")
testcollapse2<- testcollapse0
teststring0<- "testcollapse2<- collapse(testcollapse2, node=NODE)  + geom_point2(aes(subset=(node==NODE)), shape=23, size=7, fill=COLOR);"
testString2<- character()
for(i in 1:2) {
  indString<- gsub(
    pattern = "NODE",replacement =  nodes2go[i],
    x = teststring0)
  indString<- gsub(
    pattern = "COLOR", replacement = myTestCols2[i],
    x = indString)
  testString2<- c(testString2, indString)
}
rm(i, indString)
#
#Run the command
eval(parse(text = testString2))
##And now plot:
testcollapse2
#
rm(testcollapse0, testcollapse0b, testcollapse1,
   testcollapse2, teststring0, testString2)

I was wondering what would be abetter way to do it. I have tried to use drop.tip, but I may not be using it properly. Also, the advantage to use collapse on the ggtree output is that is going to work in case a node is already collapsed, which is useful in my pipeline.

Thank you for your kind attention,
Max T.
